bug.title: The real-runsc integration test wrongly requires an empty state dir, but runsc keeps one shared null-netns handle for --network=none
bug.symptoms: test_infinite_loop_is_a_timeout_and_the_state_dir_is_empty_afterward asserts the runsc --root state directory is empty once GVisorSandbox has run and cleaned up. Under the real runsc it always holds exactly one entry, "null-netns": the shared network-namespace handle runsc creates for --network=none containers. It is created once and reused — three runs leave exactly one entry, not one per container — so it is not a per-container leak. GVisorSandbox's own cleanup (runsc delete -force) removes each container's state correctly; only this shared handle remains, and the test fails on it.
bug.reproduction_steps: With runsc on PATH and NULLIUS_GVISOR_RUNTIME_ROOT set, run GVisorSandbox several times against one state_root and list it: it contains exactly ["null-netns"], regardless of how many runs.
bug.expected: - The test asserts that no per-container state remains after a run — for example that the state dir contains nothing but the shared "null-netns" handle, or that runsc lists no container — rather than requiring the directory to be wholly empty. - The infinite loop still asserts fail_class timeout. The container's own state is gone after cleanup. - Every other assertion in the file is unchanged, and the test still skips when runsc or the runtime root is absent.
bug.actual: Root cause: packages/orchestrator/tests/test_gvisor_runsc.py asserts the state directory is empty, not accounting for runsc's shared --network=none null-netns handle. GVisorSandbox cleanup is correct; the assertion is wrong.
bug.constraints: Only the one test file is edited; no production code changes No test opens a network connection or reads a real credential; the test still skips without runsc Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
